nodes.label:
Customer File Redesign — Handoff Package

Single-screen visual refresh of the customer detail sheet. **Safest possible first merge** — no DB changes, no routing changes, one component touched.

## Your workflow

```
  Claude Code → GitHub branch → Lovable auto-preview → you review → merge to main → Lovable ships prod
```

The whole point of this handoff is to keep **all experimental work on a branch** so `main` (and therefore production) is never at risk until you say so.

## How to use with Claude Code

1. Drop this folder into the repo root (or anywhere Claude Code can read it).

2. Tell Claude Code to work on a new branch, never `main`:

   > Read `handoff_customer_file/CLAUDE_CODE_BRIEF.md` and follow it exactly. Create and push the branch `customer-file-refresh` from `main`, then do all work there — never commit directly to `main`. Open a Draft PR after §2 so Lovable starts building a preview for that branch. Stop after each numbered section and show me what you did. Do not proceed to the next section until I say "continue". Do not touch any file not in the "touch list" — if you think you need to, ask me first.

3. After Claude Code finishes §2 (the legacy copy step) the branch will exist and Lovable will build a preview. Get the preview URL.

4. As Claude Code finishes each section and pushes, Lovable's preview auto-updates. Refresh the preview URL to see progress.

5. When all sections are done:
   - Open the preview with the feature flag **OFF** → everything should look like today
   - Open the preview with the feature flag **ON** → refreshed sheet should match `screenshots/02-file-open.png`
   - Walk through the test plan in §5 of the brief

6. Only after both states check out: merge the PR. Keep the Lovable production env var OFF at first. Flip it to ON for one staging dealer, watch for a day, then enable more.

## Contents

- `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIEF.md` — the single-screen spec. Keep Claude Code on these rails.
- `design_files/Customer File Redesign.html` — the approved mockup. Open it in a browser to see the exact target.
- `design_files/*.jsx`, `mock-data.js` — supporting files that make the mockup run.
- `screenshots/*.png` — reference images.

## Why start here

- **One component.** Not seven.
- **No database changes.** Nothing to roll back at the data layer.
- **No sidebar changes.** Nothing layout-wide to break.
- **Feature-flagged.** Off by default — literally zero user impact on merge until you flip the switch in Lovable env vars.
- **Fast rollback.** Flip the env var in Lovable, wait ~1 min for rebuild. Or `git revert` the merge commit.
- **Branch-isolated.** Until you merge, `main` is untouched and production is untouched.

Once this is merged and stable, the next handoff folder uses the same pattern at a larger scale.

## Safety net cheat sheet

| Worry | Answer |
|---|---|
| "What if Claude Code breaks something?" | It's on a branch. `main` is fine. Close the PR. |
| "What if the merged version breaks something?" | Flip `VITE_CUSTOMER_FILE_REFRESH=false` in Lovable env. ~1 min rebuild. |
| "What if the legacy version behind the flag is broken?" | `git revert` the merge commit. Lovable redeploys the previous state. |
| "What if Claude Code tries to touch other files?" | The brief tells it to stop and ask. If it asks, say no. If it didn't ask, the PR diff will show you — request changes on the PR. |
| "What if there's a bad DB migration?" | There isn't one in this handoff. Claude Code is instructed not to add any. If it does, reject the PR. |

## Guardrails in one sentence

If Claude Code wants to touch a file not in the "touch list", open a database migration, or "clean up" unrelated code — say **no** and point back at this brief.

Customer File Redesign — Handoff Package

Single-screen visual refresh of the customer detail sheet. **Safest possible first merge** — no DB changes, no routing changes, one component touched.

## Your workflow

```
  Claude Code → GitHub branch → Lovable auto-preview → you review → merge to main → Lovable ships prod
```

The whole point of this handoff is to keep **all experimental work on a branch** so `main` (and therefore production) is never at risk until you say so.

## How to use with Claude Code

1. Drop this folder into the repo root (or anywhere Claude Code can read it).

2. Tell Claude Code to work on a new branch, never `main`:

   > Read `handoff_customer_file/CLAUDE_CODE_BRIEF.md` and follow it exactly. Create and push the branch `customer-file-refresh` from `main`, then do all work there — never commit directly to `main`. Open a Draft PR after §2 so Lovable starts building a preview for that branch. Stop after each numbered section and show me what you did. Do not proceed to the next section until I say "continue". Do not touch any file not in the "touch list" — if you think you need to, ask me first.

3. After Claude Code finishes §2 (the legacy copy step) the branch will exist and Lovable will build a preview. Get the preview URL.

4. As Claude Code finishes each section and pushes, Lovable's preview auto-updates. Refresh the preview URL to see progress.

5. When all sections are done:
   - Open the preview with the feature flag **OFF** → everything should look like today
   - Open the preview with the feature flag **ON** → refreshed sheet should match `screenshots/02-file-open.png`
   - Walk through the test plan in §5 of the brief

6. Only after both states check out: merge the PR. Keep the Lovable production env var OFF at first. Flip it to ON for one staging dealer, watch for a day, then enable more.

## Contents

- `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIEF.md` — the single-screen spec. Keep Claude Code on these rails.
- `design_files/Customer File Redesign.html` — the approved mockup. Open it in a browser to see the exact target.
- `design_files/*.jsx`, `mock-data.js` — supporting files that make the mockup run.
- `screenshots/*.png` — reference images.

## Why start here

- **One component.** Not seven.
- **No database changes.** Nothing to roll back at the data layer.
- **No sidebar changes.** Nothing layout-wide to break.
- **Feature-flagged.** Off by default — literally zero user impact on merge until you flip the switch in Lovable env vars.
- **Fast rollback.** Flip the env var in Lovable, wait ~1 min for rebuild. Or `git revert` the merge commit.
- **Branch-isolated.** Until you merge, `main` is untouched and production is untouched.

Once this is merged and stable, the next handoff folder uses the same pattern at a larger scale.

## Safety net cheat sheet

| Worry | Answer |
|---|---|
| "What if Claude Code breaks something?" | It's on a branch. `main` is fine. Close the PR. |
| "What if the merged version breaks something?" | Flip `VITE_CUSTOMER_FILE_REFRESH=false` in Lovable env. ~1 min rebuild. |
| "What if the legacy version behind the flag is broken?" | `git revert` the merge commit. Lovable redeploys the previous state. |
| "What if Claude Code tries to touch other files?" | The brief tells it to stop and ask. If it asks, say no. If it didn't ask, the PR diff will show you — request changes on the PR. |
| "What if there's a bad DB migration?" | There isn't one in this handoff. Claude Code is instructed not to add any. If it does, reject the PR. |

## Guardrails in one sentence

If Claude Code wants to touch a file not in the "touch list", open a database migration, or "clean up" unrelated code — say **no** and point back at this brief.
